analysis.file_name: _Everything Bad, Everywhere, All At Once... Except Stocks__ Jensen Quits, Inflation Hits, & Market Splits.pdf
analysis.title: "Everything Bad, Everywhere, All At Once... Except Stocks": Jensen Quits, Inflation Hits, & Market Splits
key_insights: Stocks rallied through a week of bad macro news because positioning had already been cut. Goldman Prime data showed US fundamental long/short funds cut gross leverage by 8.7 points in the week of the midterms, the most since March 2020. Net leverage fell 3.7 points to 43.3%, a five-year low.
The S&P rose about 2% on the week and the SOX rose 10%, its best week since April. VIX fell 27% to 18.7, its biggest weekly drop in a year. Bonds took the hit instead.

Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO on Nov 12 after an admission of infidelity, reported US intelligence suspicions about his companion's ties to China, and a second reported affair. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO and ex-Synopsys CEO Harvey Jones is chair. Fourteen sell-side notes followed, with three downgrades and six target cuts.

NVDA opened down about 12% and closed down 4-5% after Vanda recorded its biggest opening retail bid ever in the stock, about 41x normal. NVDA fell about 11% on the week, its worst since April 2025. AMD rose about 30% and Broadcom 24%, so money moved between AI tickers rather than leaving AI.

NVDA's valuation is at a 13-year low. The report argues the stock's problem predates Huang: it was down six weeks in a row before this, the longest losing streak in 14 years, which it reads as a structural shift in the AI trade.

Core CPI came in hot for a third straight month, roughly double Goldman's 0.16% estimate, with only one of 70 forecasters expecting anything hotter. CPI has beaten forecasts by about 32bps cumulatively over four months with no single category contributing more than 4bps.

Fed officials turned hawkish. Waller said a 50bp December hike should be considered if core CPI came in around 0.3% or higher. Logan wants at least two more 25bp hikes, Bowman could back a December hike, and Daly, Hammack and Goolsbee also leaned toward tightening. Goldman added a third hike in March 2027, taking the peak funds rate to 4.25-4.50%, with the first cut in December 2027.

Friday's PPI showed headline producer prices up 6.5% y/y, the highest since November 2022, and core up 5.0%. Energy deflated on the month, food prices are soaring, and intermediate demand prices are running at more than double the pace of final demand, which points to more pipeline inflation.

The Treasury market sold off hard. The 2Y rose about 35bps on the week, its biggest weekly jump since October 2024, the 10Y about 28bps and the 30Y about 20bps. The 10Y is above 5.14%, about 15bps from its multi-decade high. All three refunding auctions tailed, and the 10Y indirect bid fell from 80.3% to 61.2%, the lowest since October 2023.

The move was a real-rate shock. 10-year breakevens barely moved while TIPS yields rose for a fifth straight day and are up 90bps this year, so the market is pricing tighter policy, not higher inflation.
The October federal deficit was $404bn, the worst October on record. Interest was $115.5bn, or 28.2% of federal revenue, also a record.

Credit is calm at index level (CDX IG tighter, hyperscaler CDS at one-month lows) but weak underneath. Chip CDS widened beyond hyperscaler CDS for the first time, and CCC spreads are 270bps wider in three months. CoreWeave guided to a $1.1bn quarterly interest bill on $47bn of debt, and its 2032 bonds priced at 990bps over.

Oil: Brent fell below $90 on Tuesday for the first time since August, then jumped to about $96 after Trump said "we don't need a deal" on Iran. Tankers continue to hit mines in Hormuz. The IEA said the oil market is swinging to surplus. Diesel remains above $6.

The dollar hit its highest since May 2025 and broke out of an 18-month range. USDJPY briefly broke 160 before Japan's FX chief warned moves were excessively rapid. Gold fell 4.7% to about $3,874, its first close below $4,000 in months. Bitcoin fell below $70,000, under its 200-day moving average, and ether lost about 10% on the week.

AI earnings were beat-and-raise with sell-the-news reactions where margins or funding were the concern. Cisco fell 5.6% on a 250bp gross margin drop, AMAT fell 6.6% despite record revenue, and Nebius fell 16.8%. CoreWeave rose about 25% and Cerebras jumped about 17% premarket on strong guidance. The report's read is that margins and funding are being repriced, not demand.
Anthropic launched an IPO seeking up to about $64bn at roughly $1tn market value ($1.4tn fully diluted). The book was reported about six times covered. It prices Nov 18 and trades Nov 19.

Fund flows: global equity funds drew $51.0bn, European equity funds drew $35.1bn (the most since June 2021), and US equity funds drew $6.6bn. Money market funds lost $37.5bn after the prior week's $174bn inflow.

The authors side with the bond market and expect chop with a downside skew. They argue positioning gave stocks a temporary pass that ends once shorts are covered and CTAs finish selling. Goldman's Privorotsky expects chop rather than a breakout, while JPMorgan's Market Intel desk and Goldman's equity strategists lean bullish, with a 14% S&P gain forecast over the next year.

market_movers.rationale: Goldman's James Schneider called Huang's exit a "meaningful, but measured negative", kept his $10 EPS estimate, cut the multiple from 30x to 22x and cut his target to $220.
JPMorgan's Harlan Sur cut his target to $215 after removing China from FY28 estimates. JPM's credit team stays Underweight on GPU financing risk.
Bernstein's Stacy Rasgon, long a bull, downgraded and warned that "there will no doubt be more allegations to come."
BTIG's Jonathan Krinsky says the bounce has reached his $150-155 sell zone. It could fill the October gap near $169, and a close above $175 would change his cautious view.

sector_views.rationale: Rotation from Nvidia into AMD and Broadcom drove the SOX's best week since April. BTIG calls a six-month top, while Goldman's Privorotsky says the leadership issue is not deteriorating AI demand.
Rate-sensitive sectors lagged and Energy outperformed on the week as yields surged.
The market is paying for capex suppliers (AMAT, AVGO, AMD) and discounting companies that absorb memory costs (Cisco) or finance the buildout (Nebius, Nscale).

earnings_insights: Cisco fiscal Q1 revenue reported $18.52bn (+24% y/y) and EPS $1.40 (non-GAAP, as presented). It raised its FY27 revenue guide to $74.8-75.8bn and EPS guide to $5.47-5.53, and doubled its AI infrastructure revenue target to $9bn. Non-GAAP gross margin fell 250bp to 65.6%. Product orders grew 21%. Cisco stopped breaking out hyperscaler AI orders. The stock fell 5.6% Friday.

Applied Materials reported record revenue of $10.41bn (+53% y/y) and EPS of $4.16 against a $4.06 estimate. It guided Q1 revenue to $11.1bn ± $0.5bn against $10.89bn expected, and said wafer-fab equipment demand should grow more than 30% in 2027. The stock fell 6.6% Friday.

CoreWeave reported a beat and raise on Tuesday night, guided to adjusted profitability in the first half of 2028 (per Reuters), and guided to a $1.1bn quarterly interest bill on $47bn of debt. The stock rose 24.7% Wednesday.

Cerebras guided Q4 core revenue to $310-330mn against $271.2mn expected, with new deals with Oracle and Microsoft. The stock rose about 17% premarket. Nebius guided capex up and outlook down and fell 16.8% Thursday.
Nvidia reports Tuesday, Nov 17 (Kress's first print as interim CEO) against a $108bn guide. The stock trades at roughly 10x Goldman's 2027 earnings.
S&P earnings growth is forecast by Goldman strategists to slow to 11% in 2027 from 36% in 2026.

macro_indicators.interpretation: A third straight hot core print, with strength in medical services and insurance as well as energy. It raised the odds of a faster Fed pace.
Goldman's pre-print estimate, which the actual print roughly doubled.
The highest since November 2022. It pushed 2027 pricing to 50/50 for two or three more hikes.
Intermediate demand prices are running at more than twice the pace of final demand, pointing to more pipeline inflation and margin pressure.
The worst October on record. Interest of $115.5bn is 28.2% of federal revenue.
Goldman's forecast after adding a third hike in March 2027, with the first cut in December 2027.
About 15bps from its multi-decade high. The move reflects real yields, not breakevens.

macro_indicators.reading: 10% chance of 50bps; 70% chance of another 25bps in January
macro_indicators.interpretation: Market pricing as cited from Nomura, reflecting the hawkish Fedspeak.
Whipsawed between below $90 and $96 on Iran headlines. The IEA says the market is swinging to surplus.
Builds the case for a December BoJ hike.

crypto_views: Bitcoin rallied with the Nasdaq on Wednesday, then fell to about $71,400 on Thursday, its lowest close since mid-August, and slid below $70,000 on Friday, under its 200-day moving average. It is down almost 6% on the week.
Ether lost about 10% on the week. The report describes bitcoin as acting like a high-beta tech stock.
The report links the weakness in crypto to rising real yields and a stronger dollar, and asks whether retail money went into the Anthropic IPO instead.
risk_factors: Real yields keep rising, with the 10Y above 5% and about 15bps from its multi-decade high. Foreign demand at Treasury auctions has weakened.
A Fed that wants to move faster, including a possible 50bp hike in December. Stocks are not priced for it, per the authors.
Positioning support fades once shorts are covered and CTAs finish selling.
Nvidia's first earnings without Huang on Nov 17, and further allegations or investigations (DOJ antitrust probe, congressional testimony, financing deals).
AI funding strain: a roughly $33bn funding gap next year, 55GW of new capacity coming through 2028, and CCC spreads near cycle wides.
Yen intervention risk at USDJPY 160, which could unwind yen-funded trades. BofA's stress index shows Japan as the most stressed region.
Renewed US strikes on Iran and mine attacks in Hormuz, with oil's war premium largely priced out.
A weak Anthropic IPO could become the next clearing event for the AI trade.
vol_and_positioning: VIX was above 25 the prior Friday, briefly traded into the 20s after CPI, and ended the week at 18.7, down 27%, its biggest weekly drop in a year. Goldman's Privorotsky read the failure to sustain a vol premium as a sign that positioning is supporting the tape.

Goldman's Coppersmith: the realized volatility of VVIX hit an all-time high over 5 and 10 days. Last Thursday saw 55.8 million puts trade across US venues, the most ever, followed by one of the fastest dumps of protection on record.
Goldman's vol desk: the street is structurally short vol on the way down and long vol on the way up, which should create an asymmetric bid for protection on any meaningful selloff.
Nomura's McElligott called Monday's move "an absolutely epic vol crush" with dealers forced to buy on the way up.

Goldman Prime: net leverage at 43.3% is a five-year low, and clients net sold more than $30bn of tech since the unwind began, versus $21bn in July. Semis positioning had almost fully round-tripped in 2026.

Systematic long/short funds had their best two days in almost three years. Buyback desks are running at 1.6x last year's pace, with record authorizations of $1.5tn year to date. CTAs are expected to sell about $31bn of S&P futures regardless of direction and remain sellers on a flat or falling tape.

JPMorgan's Market Intel desk says the market feels "coil-sprung to go higher" (the pain trade), but concedes most of the past month's move was short covering. Retail buying in Nvidia ran at roughly nine standard deviations on Thursday morning.
Three sub-$4 stocks made up 32% of US tape volume on Wednesday, and Goldman's Retail Favorites basket had one of its best days in three years.
geopolitical: Iran: Trump said "we don't need a deal" and shut the door on talks. Tankers are hitting mines in Hormuz almost daily, the IRGC struck navigation equipment on Oman's Didamar Island, and a third US carrier group is reportedly on its way.

US-China: US intelligence suspected Alice Huang of ties to China's Ministry of State Security. The DOJ is examining whether she helped smuggle Super Micro products to China, and Bloomberg reported a Chinese company founded by her procured smuggled AI chips. Trump meets Xi at APEC in Shenzhen on Nov 18-19. Fears of tighter US chip curbs hit the Hang Seng Tech index.

US midterms: The report refers to the AI trade crashing after the midterms. Democrats take over Congress, and Trump wants Senate Republicans to pass a $350bn military reconciliation bill before then, with a Dec 11 funding deadline.
Data-center politics: Josh Hawley became the first Republican senator to back a national data-center moratorium, while a bipartisan permitting bill cleared a Senate procedural vote 73-25.
Brazil: a post-election rout continues, with the real at its weakest since June 2025 as Lula weighs new fiscal measures.
cross_bank_references: Goldman's equity strategists lean into the dip with a 14% S&P forecast, while the authors side with the bond market.
JPMorgan's Market Intel desk calls the market coil-sprung to go higher, while Goldman's Privorotsky expects chop rather than a breakout.
BTIG's Krinsky is cautious on semis and calls a six-month top, while Goldman's Privorotsky says leadership uncertainty is not deteriorating AI demand.
Goldman's Schneider cuts NVDA to $220 and Bernstein's Rasgon downgrades, while retail bought the opening dip at 41x normal volume (Vanda).
Nomura matches Goldman in adding a hike: Nomura also expects a third hike in the Fed's path.

tension_points.bull_case: Positioning is a tailwind. Net leverage is at a five-year low, buybacks are running at 1.6x last year's pace, and Goldman's strategists forecast a 14% S&P gain over the next year. JPMorgan's Market Intel desk says the market feels coil-sprung to go higher.
tension_points.bear_case: The bond market priced a hawkish Fed: the 2Y rose 35bps, the 10Y is above 5.14%, and real yields are rising. The authors say a short-covering rally cannot offset tighter financial conditions forever, and CTAs remain sellers on a flat or falling tape.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Stocks are being supported by short covering; the bear case weakens if Tuesday's retail sales and industrial production are soft and the Fed backs away from a 50bp December hike. The 10Y moving above its multi-decade high near 5.29% (about 15bps above current) would strengthen it.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman's Privorotsky says leadership uncertainty is not the same as deteriorating AI demand. Retail bid the stock at 41x normal volume and the stock trades at roughly 10x Goldman's 2027 earnings.
tension_points.bear_case: Rasgon warns of more allegations, there are DOJ and congressional probes, and Kress has reportedly pushed back on Huang's financing deals. The stock was down six weeks in a row before the resignation, which the authors read as a structural shift.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Nvidia's Nov 17 earnings: the numbers matter less than whether the company sounds like it can run without its founder.

tension_points.bull_case: The SOX had its best week since April as money rotated from Nvidia into AMD and Broadcom, and capex suppliers are being rewarded.
tension_points.bear_case: BTIG's Krinsky called a six-month top in semis and says the bounce has reached his $150-155 SOXX sell zone with limited upside beyond the $169 gap fill. SOXX reversed lower on Friday.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A close above $175 in SOXX would cause BTIG to rethink its cautious posture.

theme_stances.key_argument: Forced sellers finished last week, so this week's bad news landed on a market with no one left to sell.
theme_stances.evidence: positioning may now be doing more to support the tape

theme_stances.theme: hawkish Fed and rising real yields
theme_stances.key_argument: A real-rate shock and a Fed talking about 50bp are tightening financial conditions that a short-covering rally cannot offset forever.
theme_stances.evidence: We side with the bond market.

theme_stances.key_argument: Money did not leave AI but moved from Nvidia into AMD and Broadcom, with capex suppliers rewarded.
theme_stances.evidence: the money didn't leave AI, it just changed tickers
